strengths: Well-articulated motivation: Compelling case for why unifying perception, planning, and generation within a single VLM avoids text-only bottlenecks and enables bidirectional information/gradient flow. The motivation is clearly presented and conceptually sound.

Comprehensive experimental validation: Thorough evaluation on Bench2Drive including closed-loop metrics (DS, SR, efficiency, comfortness), open-loop metrics (L2 error, collision rate), 3D detection metrics (mAP, mATE, mASE, etc.), and VQA performance. The breadth of metrics strengthens the empirical case.

Consistent improvements across multiple dimensions: 5.9% improvement in L2 trajectory error, 9.2% in collision rate over ORION; FID scores of 6.4-7.1 on image generation; improved mAP and NDS; better multi-ability performance across diverse scenarios.

Thoughtful technical design: Two complementary image generation paradigms (discrete AR vs. continuous AR+Diffusion) with honest analysis of trade-offs. The coupling of planning and generation via token placement, flow-matching loss, and CLIP-based semantic alignment are well-considered.

Rigorous ablation studies: Table 4 effectively isolates contributions of detection head, planning head, and image generation module. Table 6 and supplementary comparisons between AR variants provide valuable insights.
Clear presentation: Well-structured paper with effective figures (especially Fig. 1 and 3). The progression from motivation through method to results is logical and easy to follow.
Two-stage training strategy: Preserving VQA capability while adding new tasks shows practical consideration for maintaining model versatility.
Reproducibility details: Includes training details, hyperparameters, dataset split information, and code availability mentioned.
weaknesses: Limited to simulation environments: Evaluation only on Bench2Drive (CARLA v2), a closed-loop simulator. No validation on real-world datasets (nuScenes, Waymo, Argoverse). Generalization to real driving with different weather, lighting, and distribution shifts is unverified and crucial for autonomous driving applications.

Questionable design choices with insufficient justification: (1) Omitting KL regularization in trajectory planner VAE justified only by 'empirical instability' without evidence or analysis; (2) Resolution selection (192×128 for AR, 256×256 for AR+Diffusion) appears arbitrary with no ablation; (3) Using 'deterministic reconstruction' in AR+Diffusion defeats the stochasticity of diffusion models with no analysis of whether this is necessary.

Incremental technical novelty: Individual components largely build on existing work (QT-Former from ORION, LoRA fine-tuning, flow-matching). While integration is novel, the contribution is primarily architectural rather than algorithmic. The main insight—that joint optimization helps—is intuitive but lacks theoretical grounding.

Incomplete ablation and analysis: (1) No ablation isolating the contribution of trajectory-conditioned generation vs. auxiliary supervision signal; (2) No analysis of scenario-specific failures or when joint optimization might harm individual tasks; (3) Missing cross-component interaction analysis.

Computational cost and deployment feasibility not addressed: Training requires 8×H200 GPUs; no inference time, memory overhead, or real-world deployment analysis provided. This is critical information for practical applications in autonomous driving.

Single-benchmark evaluation with potential distribution bias: Training and validation both on Bench2Drive base set (950/50 split). No cross-dataset validation or evaluation on held-out test sets from other simulators/real-world data. Improvements could reflect dataset-specific overfitting.

Statistical rigor lacking: No error bars, confidence intervals, or multi-run variance analysis. Single-run results without significance testing. This is particularly important given the relatively modest improvements (5-9%).

Limited comparison scope: No adaptation/comparison of other recent unified models (Janus, Metamorph, BLIP-3 family) to driving. FSDrive comparison limited mainly to FID; other metric comparisons would strengthen claims of superiority.

Missing analysis of failure modes: No discussion of when predictions become inconsistent, diverge from ground truth, or violate constraints. No analysis of edge cases or adversarial scenarios in simulation.

Unclear contribution of future image prediction to planning: While ablation (Table 4) shows removing image generation hurts planning, the mechanism is not clear. Is it auxiliary supervision, the additional regularization, or genuine information flow? The paper doesn't provide sufficient insight into why joint optimization works.
